teas.name: Farmer Chang's Honey Black
teas.description: Called "Honey Fragrance" black tea in Taiwan, this tea brews up notes of honey and cinnamon in a lighter but smooth and flavorful cup. Single steep 3-5 min.
teas.notes: Strong and malty; very enjoyable but don't oversteep. Good only for a single steep.

teas.name: Farmer Lee's Red Jade Black
teas.description: Red Jade is in a class of its own and must be approached on what it brings to the table. Think of it as a fine dark Taiwanese Oolong. It's lighter in body and not as malty as Formosa Assam but sweeter, more delicate and with a cleaner finish.
teas.notes: Particular taste hard to describe; may be a little off putting.

teas.name: Himalayan Gold Black Tea
teas.description: Robust, Rich & Flavory Loose Tea. Radiant blend from the Eastern Himalayas with shiny golden tips, high caffeine, and a delicate aroma.

teas.name: Dian Hong Black
teas.description: You'll find it to be a classic, delicious black tea - nice mouthfeel, a bit malty and only slightly dry.

teas.name: Chi Lai High Mountain Black
teas.description: A high mountain black tea grown at elevation on Chi Lai Mountain in Hualien County. Clean, bright, and delicately sweet with a smooth mouthfeel and none of the bitterness of lowland blacks.

teas.name: Alpine Honey Red
teas.description: A red tea (black tea) grown at alpine elevation in Taiwan, carrying natural honey notes from the high-mountain terroir. Light-bodied and sweet with a clean, lingering finish.

teas.name: Asian Beauty Oolong
teas.description: On the darker side of the Oolong spectrum is our Asian Beauty, a smooth, sweet, and fragrant Oolong - and Taiwan's most famous "bug-bitten" tea. This tea is only produced in the Summer when the leaves naturally acquire notes of honey and cinnamon from the little leaf hoppers.
teas.notes: Very pleasant richer oolong. Benefits from a gongfu steeping but depletes pretty rapidly.

teas.name: High Mountain Honey Oolong
teas.description: Farmer Luo makes this small-batch, hand-made tea in the Alishan growing region only once per year in the Summer.
teas.notes: A little lighter than expected. Great entry into oolongs if you're coming from heavy blacks. Benefits from a gongfu steeping.

teas.name: Dong Ding Oolong - Heavy Roast
teas.description: Dong Ding Oolong masterfully roasted by a friend of ours in Taichung. If you like roasted oolongs, this is a great choice! Make sure to rinse this one first.

teas.name: 2012 Roasted Tieguanyin
teas.description: It has been said that this is a tea that is close to coffee. But who wants coffee? Other reviews have said it is like walking in a Redwood forest. Worth trying.

teas.name: Honey Black Oolong (Spring 2026)
teas.description: A spring 2026 harvest black oolong from Taiwan. Processed with high oxidation to yield a naturally sweet honey aroma, rich and smooth body, and a warming finish.

teas.name: Alishan Firefly Milk Oolong (Winter Pick)
teas.description: A winter harvest milk oolong from the celebrated Alishan high mountain region. The Firefly varietal produces a naturally creamy, buttery character with floral high notes and a lingering sweet finish.

teas.name: Sweet Assamica Red Oolong
teas.description: A red oolong crafted from the large-leaf Assamica cultivar, processed with significant oxidation for a rich, full-bodied sweetness. Smooth and approachable with ripe fruit and honey notes.

teas.name: Acacia Charcoal Roast Milk Oolong
teas.description: A milk oolong roasted over acacia charcoal, adding a warm, lightly toasty complexity to the naturally creamy base. Deep and satisfying, with excellent multi-steep character.

teas.name: Twisted Green
teas.description: Aromatic, nutty and crisp! If you've never had fresh green tea straight from the fields you owe it to yourself to try this.
teas.notes: A bit grassy; optimal steep still hasn't presented itself but would steer away from gongfu.

teas.name: Green Tea of the Clouds
teas.description: If you are a fan of our own Twisted Green, this "Green Tea of the Clouds" is highly recommended as it's similar in the inhale and taste profile but more delicate and even smoother.

teas.name: Himalayan Green
teas.description: High Elevation Grown Green Tea Leaves From Himalayas | Pure Unblended Single Origin Green Loose.
teas.notes: A bit grassy, haven't found the good balance of steep time/water ratio.

teas.name: Sencha Shin-ryoku
teas.description: Premium sencha grown at high elevation in the prestigious tea region of Honyama. First flush, Yabukita cultivar. Well-balanced between flavor and body with a natural sweetness.

teas.name: Organic Fukamushi Sencha
teas.description: Traditional deep-steamed (fukamushi) sencha from Kakegawa. Carefully deep steamed for mild, aromatic flavor. Grown under JAS organic certification. Mild with fresh grassy and earthy aromas.

teas.name: Gyokuro Kin
teas.description: A cup of affordable luxury. Shade-grown gyokuro from Asahina with the elegance of famed gyokuro teas. Gentle bitterness and umami mouthfeel that progressively becomes slightly sweet and astringent.

teas.name: Moonlight Earl Grey
teas.description: Earl Grey 'cream' blend. Comforting flavors of vanilla and cream combine to soften the citrus notes of traditional Earl Grey.
teas.notes: Consider softening with a basic black like daily darjeeling.

teas.name: Cream
teas.description: Sweet, inviting and warm, with a delicate creamy consistency and aroma of fresh black tea. Pleasantly brisk and very refreshing.
teas.notes: Consider softening with a basic black like daily darjeeling.

teas.name: Masala Chai
teas.description: Premium Ceylon black tea with cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and ginger. In Indian culture, 'Masala' means 'a blend of spices'.
teas.notes: Very heavy on the spice. Consider softening with a basic black like daily darjeeling and perhaps even (perish the thought) milk and a sweetener.

teas.name: Sakura Ryokucha
teas.description: Seasonal blend of sencha, kukicha, sakura leaves and sakura flowers. Sakura flowers preserved in sugar for a subtle sweetness without affecting the tea flavor.
teas.notes: Very strong cherry blossom notes; not to my liking.

teas.name: Decaf Ceylon
teas.description: Classic black tea from the island of Sri Lanka. Clean, tangy aroma, medium body, with sweet citrus notes like mandarin, and refreshing astringency.

teas.name: Decaf Metz Organic Blue Nile Chamomile
Daily Darjeeling
teas.description: Well rounded with some muscatel notes. This is a basic black tea. Nice with a straight steep or as a mixer to dampen some of the strong flavored teas.

teas.name: "Mixiang" Honey Red Oolong
teas.description: Red Oolong is something of a rage these days in Taiwan. It's made by fermenting the leaves as far as possible without becoming a black tea. It's distinguished by a nice reddish amber color to the tea and smooth drinkability.
teas.notes: Only had this in sample and now it is sold out. Should be on the lookout for the next iteration.
